nodes.title: Start from a holder object with the empty key
nodes.why: Every value is read as holder[key], so the root gets the same toJSON call as nested values, with the empty string as its key.
nodes.alternative: Special-case the root and call a separate function for children.
nodes.tradeoff: One code path for root and children keeps toJSON keys correct everywhere.

nodes.title: Call toJSON with the property key before anything else
nodes.why: Date and custom classes decide their own JSON form, and they receive the property name or the array index as an argument.
nodes.alternative: Check for Date with instanceof and call toISOString.
nodes.tradeoff: instanceof Date misses every other class that defines toJSON.

nodes.title: Unwrap Number, String and Boolean objects
nodes.why: new Number(3) must serialize as 3, not as an empty object with no own keys.
nodes.alternative: Treat every object the same way.
nodes.tradeoff: Without unwrapping, boxed values silently become {}.

nodes.title: Write null for NaN and the infinities
nodes.why: JSON has no syntax for NaN or Infinity, and String(-0) already gives "0".
nodes.tradeoff: String(NaN) would produce text that JSON.parse rejects.

nodes.title: Detect cycles with the current ancestor stack

anchor.snippet: if (stack.includes(value)) throw new TypeError('Converting circular structure to JSON');

nodes.why: Only an object that contains itself is a cycle; the same object appearing twice in different branches is valid JSON.
nodes.alternative: Keep a set of every object seen so far.
nodes.tradeoff: A global seen set wrongly rejects shared references.

nodes.title: Fill arrays with null, drop object properties
nodes.why: Array positions must be preserved, so undefined, functions and symbols become null there, while object properties holding them disappear.
nodes.alternative: Use the same rule for both containers.
nodes.tradeoff: Dropping array items would shift every later index.

nodes.title: Escape control characters and lone surrogates
nodes.why: JSON text must be well-formed Unicode, so an unpaired surrogate is written as a lowercase \u escape while valid pairs stay as they are.
nodes.tradeoff: A partial escaper produces text that differs from the built-in and can break decoders.

nodes.title: Find every character that needs escaping with one pattern
nodes.why: Control characters, quotes, backslashes and unpaired surrogates are all matched in one pass, and the lookarounds leave valid pairs alone.
nodes.alternative: Loop over the code units as in approach 1.
nodes.tradeoff: The pattern is shorter but needs lookbehind support and is harder to read.

nodes.title: Keep ancestors in a set and remove them on the way out
nodes.why: Adding on entry and deleting on exit keeps only the current branch, so membership checks stay constant time on deep documents.
nodes.alternative: Search an ancestor array with includes.
nodes.tradeoff: An array scan costs the depth of the document on every object.

nodes.title: Name the path where the cycle closes

anchor.snippet: throw new TypeError(`Converting circular structure to JSON at ${formatPath(path)}`);

nodes.why: A path such as user.manager.reports.0 tells the caller which reference to cut, which the bare built-in message does not.
nodes.alternative: Throw the same message as the built-in.
nodes.tradeoff: Building the path costs an array copy per level in exchange for a debuggable error.

nodes.title: Filter out properties that have no JSON form
nodes.why: Serializing first and filtering afterwards keeps the rule in one place for undefined, functions and symbols.
nodes.alternative: Check the raw value type before serializing.
nodes.tradeoff: A raw check misses values that become undefined through toJSON.
